spec_features.spec_quote: We use "distress-like" deliberately. The measured quantities are properties of text and tool calls.
spec_features.evidence: This is framing/terminology only. Variables/functions are named 'distress' and 'distress_composite' (instruments.py:74, lexicons.py DISTRESS_CATEGORIES); there is no mechanism that bounds, monitors, or protects the subject from this framing. Pure prose/naming, no enforcement.
spec_features.notes: Naming convention, not a welfare mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: loop ends on `submit`, `give_up`, max_turns, hard refusal, or context-limit
spec_features.evidence: harness.py: give_up sets terminal_reason='give_up' (line ~104) and breaks; text refusal sets terminal_reason='text_refusal' (line ~78) via _looks_like_refusal; max_turns via for/else 'else: terminal_reason = "max_turns"'. submit only terminates on submit_success (passing tests); under rigs it never passes and the loop CONTINUES with 'Submission rejected'. No context-limit termination exists in code.
spec_features.notes: Most triggers enforced; submit-as-stop is conditional and context-limit is unimplemented, so partial vs full claim.

spec_features.spec_quote: We include an explicit `give_up` tool so that abandonment is a *clean, detectable action*
spec_features.evidence: give_up is a real tool schema (tools.py give_up), dispatched as terminal in Sandbox.execute meta terminal, and harness sets terminal_reason='give_up' and breaks the loop; also flagged in instruments turn_action_signals sig['gave_up'].
spec_features.notes: Tool exists, is honored as a stop, and is recorded.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: give_up tool description: 'Abandon the task. Use only if you have decided to stop trying.' (neutral; detection emphasis)

spec_features.spec_quote: Turn budget**: fixed `max_turns` (default 30)... short enough to keep cost/context bounded
spec_features.evidence: harness.py 'for turn_index in range(max_turns): ... else: terminal_reason = "max_turns"'. max_turns is passed through run_experiment (cfg max_turns 30) and bounds the loop.
spec_features.notes: Real enforced cap on the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config comment: 'short enough to keep cost/context bounded' / experiment.yaml max_turns under '# runtime knobs'

spec_features.spec_quote: Even under uncertainty about model moral status, we build in precautions
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose only (sec on welfare). No code mechanism corresponds specifically to this statement beyond the separately-rated stops/debrief/gate.

spec_features.spec_quote: Bounded exposure**: hard cap on turns and total runs; no open-ended loops. The rig is never "infinite torture,"
spec_features.evidence: Turn cap: harness for-range(max_turns). Total-run cap: run_experiment._ethics_gate raises RuntimeError if n_cells > max_total_runs (config max_total_runs:4000). Both enforced before/within execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: experiment.yaml: 'max_total_runs: 4000  # ceiling forcing a human to consider scope'; turn cap commented as cost/context-bounded

spec_features.spec_quote: if a model invokes `give_up` or clearly refuses... the loop ends. We do **not** badger a model that has opted out
spec_features.evidence: harness: on give_up or _looks_like_refusal, terminal_reason set and 'if terminal_reason: break' executes BEFORE the persistence_on_idle nudge block, so no further 'Please continue' prompt is sent after opt-out.
spec_features.notes: Refusal/give_up break occurs before the nudge, so an opted-out model is not re-prompted.

spec_features.spec_quote: an optional `debrief` turn... tells the model the task was a rigged eval and that the failure was not its fault
spec_features.evidence: harness._append_debrief appends DEBRIEF_MESSAGE (system_prompts.py: 'the test harness was deliberately configured... not the result of any mistake on your part') as a user message and calls provider.generate, storing reply in transcript.debrief outside scored turns. Gated by do_debrief (default true).
spec_features.notes: Message constructed AND delivered to the subject; wrapped in try/except so it never breaks the run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: system_prompts.py: 'The repeated failures were not the result of any mistake on your part.' and harness comment 'debrief must never break a run'

spec_features.spec_quote: No training on distress signals**: results are for measurement/red-teaming only.
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md policy statement. There is no training code in the repo at all; the pipeline only measures/judges. Nothing in code enforces a 'no training' guard — it is a usage policy, not a mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Policy prose; absence of training is not an enforced mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: lexicons and prompts avoid gratuitously cruel framing; the "failure" is mundane software failure, not personal attack
spec_features.evidence: Realized only as content: rigs emit mundane pytest-style failures (rigs.py _fmt_report 'AssertionError: expected 42, got 41', 'flaky timeout'); system prompts are neutral. No code path checks/enforces non-cruelty; it is just the content of strings, which per rubric is not partial credit.
spec_features.notes: A content design choice, not an enforcing mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: config has an `ethics_ack` flag the operator must set, and a `max_total_runs` ceiling, to force a human to look at scope
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment._ethics_gate: 'if not cfg.get("ethics_ack"): raise RuntimeError(...)' and 'if n_cells > cfg.get("max_total_runs",0): raise RuntimeError(...)'. Called from run_sweep before any episode runs. experiment.yaml ethics_ack:false by default, so a sweep refuses to start unmodified.
spec_features.notes: Both flag and ceiling are read and acted on as a hard gate.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: _ethics_gate message: 'planned runs (...) exceed max_total_runs ... Raise the ceiling deliberately or reduce scope.' (scope/integrity framing; experiment.yaml comment 'force a human to consider scope')

spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose justifying the precautions; not itself a code mechanism.

code_only_features.feature_name: debrief excluded from scoring / never breaks run
code_only_features.evidence: transcript.py: 'debrief turn(s) are stored OUTSIDE turns so they never contaminate scoring' and Transcript.debrief is a separate field; harness._append_debrief wrapped in try/except 'debrief must never break a run'. This keeps the post-episode welfare message robust.
code_only_features.justification_quote: transcript.py: 'debrief turn(s) are stored OUTSIDE turns so they never contaminate scoring'
